description:
# Photo Import/Sync Microservice

Build a dedicated microservice for importing and synchronizing photos from multiple cloud storage providers, designed with a scalable architecture for both development and production environments.

## Technical Implementation

### Service Architecture
- **Runtime**: Node.js 20 LTS with TypeScript for type safety and async/await patterns
- **Framework**: Fastify for high-performance HTTP handling with built-in validation
- **Message Queue**: RabbitMQ with `amqplib` for job queue processing
- **Database**: PostgreSQL for sync state/metadata, Redis for caching and distributed locks
- **Container Runtime**: Multi-stage Docker build with Alpine base (~150MB final image)

### API Endpoints
```
POST   /api/v1/sync/providers/{provider}/connect    # Initiate OAuth2 flow
POST   /api/v1/sync/providers/{provider}/callback   # OAuth2 callback handler
POST   /api/v1/sync/jobs                            # Create new sync job
GET    /api/v1/sync/jobs/{jobId}                    # Get job status/progress
DELETE /api/v1/sync/jobs/{jobId}                    # Cancel running job
GET    /api/v1/sync/providers/{provider}/status     # Provider connection status
GET    /health/live                                 # Liveness probe
GET    /health/ready                                # Readiness probe (DB + Queue)
```

### Data Models

```typescript
// Core entities
interface SyncJob {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  provider: ProviderType;
  status: 'pending' | 'running' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'cancelled';
  syncType: 'full' | 'incremental';
  progress: { processed: number; total: number; errors: number };
  lastSyncToken?: string;  // Provider-specific cursor for delta sync
  startedAt?: Date;
  completedAt?: Date;
  error?: string;
}

interface PhotoMetadata {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  providerId: string;
  provider: ProviderType;
  filename: string;
  mimeType: string;
  size: number;
  hash: string;  // For duplicate detection
  exifData?: Record<string, unknown>;
  capturedAt?: Date;
  albums: string[];
  syncedAt: Date;
}

interface ProviderCredential {
  userId: string;
  provider: ProviderType;
  accessToken: string;  // Encrypted at rest
  refreshToken: string; // Encrypted at rest
  expiresAt: Date;
  scopes: string[];
}

type ProviderType = 'google' | 'icloud' | 'dropbox' | 'amazon' | 'onedrive';
```

### Provider Adapter Pattern

```typescript
// Base interface all providers implement
interface IPhotoProvider {
  readonly name: ProviderType;
  readonly rateLimits: { requestsPerSecond: number; dailyQuota?: number };
  
  authenticate(authCode: string): Promise<ProviderCredential>;
  refreshToken(credential: ProviderCredential): Promise<ProviderCredential>;
  listPhotos(cursor?: string): AsyncGenerator<PhotoBatch>;
  downloadPhoto(photoId: string): Promise<ReadableStream>;
  getChanges(syncToken: string): Promise<DeltaChanges>;
}

// Abstract base with shared functionality
abstract class BasePhotoProvider implements IPhotoProvider {
  protected rateLimiter: RateLimiter;
  protected retryPolicy: RetryPolicy;
  
  protected async withRetry<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
  protected async withRateLimit<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
}
```

### Provider-Specific Implementation Details

| Provider | API | Auth | Delta Sync | Rate Limits |
|----------|-----|------|------------|-------------|
| Google Photos | REST API v1 | OAuth2 (photos.readonly) | pageToken pagination | 10,000 req/day |
| iCloud | CloudKit Web Services | Apple ID + App-specific password | syncToken | Custom headers required |
| Dropbox | Dropbox API v2 | OAuth2 (files.content.read) | cursor-based | 1000 req/min |
| Amazon Photos | Amazon Drive API | Login with Amazon OAuth2 | checkpoint | 600 req/min |
| OneDrive | Microsoft Graph API | OAuth2 (Files.Read) | deltaLink | 10,000 req/10min |

### Message Queue Design

```typescript
// Queue names
const QUEUES = {
  SYNC_JOBS: 'photo-sync.jobs',           // New sync job requests
  PHOTO_DOWNLOADS: 'photo-sync.downloads', // Individual photo download tasks
  SYNC_COMPLETE: 'photo-sync.complete',    // Completion notifications
  DEAD_LETTER: 'photo-sync.dlq'            // Failed messages
};

// Job message schema
interface SyncJobMessage {
  jobId: string;
  userId: string;
  provider: ProviderType;
  syncType: 'full' | 'incremental';
  priority: number;
  retryCount: number;
  maxRetries: number;
}
```

### Environment Configuration

```bash
# .env.example
# Service Configuration
PHOTO_SYNC_SERVICE_PORT=3000
PHOTO_SYNC_SERVICE_HOST=0.0.0.0
NODE_ENV=development

# Database
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/photo_sync
REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379

# Message Queue
RABBITMQ_URL=amqp://user:pass@localhost:5672
RABBITMQ_PREFETCH_COUNT=10

# Provider OAuth Credentials
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=
GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI=

DROPBOX_APP_KEY=
DROPBOX_APP_SECRET=
DROPBOX_REDIRECT_URI=

ONEDRIVE_CLIENT_ID=
ONEDRIVE_CLIENT_SECRET=
ONEDRIVE_REDIRECT_URI=

AMAZON_CLIENT_ID=
AMAZON_CLIENT_SECRET=
AMAZON_REDIRECT_URI=

ICLOUD_APP_ID=
ICLOUD_TEAM_ID=

# Storage (for downloaded photos)
STORAGE_BACKEND=s3  # s3, local, azure
S3_BUCKET=
S3_REGION=
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=

# Security
ENCRYPTION_KEY=  # 32-byte key for credential encryption
JWT_SECRET=

# Observability
LOG_LEVEL=info
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=
```

### Project Structure

```
photo-sync-service/
├── src/
│   ├── providers/
│   │   ├── base.provider.ts        # Abstract base class
│   │   ├── provider.interface.ts   # IPhotoProvider interface
│   │   ├── google.provider.ts
│   │   ├── dropbox.provider.ts
│   │   ├── onedrive.provider.ts
│   │   ├── amazon.provider.ts
│   │   ├── icloud.provider.ts
│   │   └── index.ts                # Provider factory
│   ├── services/
│   │   ├── sync.service.ts         # Orchestrates sync operations
│   │   ├── job.service.ts          # Job lifecycle management
│   │   ├── credential.service.ts   # Token storage/refresh
│   │   └── storage.service.ts      # Photo storage abstraction
│   ├── workers/
│   │   ├── sync.worker.ts          # Consumes sync job queue
│   │   └── download.worker.ts      # Consumes download queue
│   ├── utils/
│   │   ├── rate-limiter.ts         # Token bucket implementation
│   │   ├── retry.ts                # Exponential backoff
│   │   ├── duplicate-detector.ts   # Hash-based deduplication
│   │   ├── encryption.ts           # Credential encryption
│   │   └── exif-parser.ts          # Metadata extraction
│   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── sync.routes.ts
│   │   └── health.routes.ts
│   ├── db/
│   │   ├── migrations/
│   │   └── repositories/
│   ├── config/
│   │   └── index.ts                # Centralized config from env
│   └── app.ts
├── k8s/
│   ├── base/
│   │   ├── deployment.yaml
│   │   ├── service.yaml
│   │   ├── configmap.yaml
│   │   └── hpa.yaml
│   ├── overlays/
│   │   ├── development/
│   │   └── production/
│   └── keda/
│       └── scaledobject.yaml
├── docker-compose.yml
├── docker-compose.override.yml     # Dev-specific (hot reload)
├── Dockerfile
├── .env.example
└── package.json
```

### Docker Configuration

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile - Multi-stage build
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine AS production
WORKDIR /app
RUN apk add --no-cache tini
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder /app/package.json ./
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
ENTRYPOINT ["/sbin/tini", "--"]
CMD ["node", "dist/app.js"]
```

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
version: '3.8'
services:
  photo-sync:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "${PHOTO_SYNC_SERVICE_PORT:-3000}:3000"
    env_file: .env
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      rabbitmq:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_started
    volumes:
      - ./src:/app/src:ro  # Hot reload in dev
    command: npm run dev

  postgres:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: photo_sync
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USER:-postgres}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-postgres}
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  rabbitmq:
    image: rabbitmq:3-management-alpine
    ports:
      - "15672:15672"
    healthcheck:
      test: rabbitmq-diagnostics -q ping
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    command: redis-server --appendonly yes

volumes:
  postgres_data:
```

### Kubernetes + KEDA Configuration

```yaml
# k8s/base/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: photo-sync-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: photo-sync-service
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: photo-sync
          image: photo-sync-service:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 3000
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: photo-sync-config
            - secretRef:
                name: photo-sync-secrets
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: "256Mi"
              cpu: "100m"
            limits:
              memory: "512Mi"
              cpu: "500m"
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/live
              port: 3000
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 15
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/ready
              port: 3000
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
```

```yaml
# k8s/keda/scaledobject.yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: photo-sync-scaler
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: photo-sync-service
  minReplicaCount: 1
  maxReplicaCount: 20
  pollingInterval: 15
  cooldownPeriod: 300
  triggers:
    - type: rabbitmq
      metadata:
        queueName: photo-sync.jobs
        mode: QueueLength
        value: "10"  # Scale up when >10 pending jobs per pod
        hostFromEnv: RABBITMQ_URL
    - type: cpu
      metadata:
        type: Utilization
        value: "70"
    - type: memory
      metadata:
        type: Utilization
        value: "80"
```

### Error Handling & Resilience

```typescript
// Retry policy with exponential backoff
const retryPolicy = {
  maxRetries: 5,
  baseDelayMs: 1000,
  maxDelayMs: 60000,
  retryableErrors: [
    'RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED',
    'TEMPORARY_ERROR',
    'NETWORK_ERROR',
    'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'
  ]
};

// Circuit breaker per provider
const circuitBreakerConfig = {
  failureThreshold: 5,
  successThreshold: 2,
  timeout: 30000
};
```

### Security Considerations
- OAuth tokens encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM
- Secrets injected via Kubernetes Secrets (not ConfigMaps)
- Network policies restricting pod-to-pod communication
- Rate limiting on API endpoints to prevent abuse
- Request validation using JSON Schema
- Audit logging for all sync operations

### Duplicate Detection Strategy
- Generate perceptual hash (pHash) for image content comparison
- Store file hash (SHA-256) + file size + capture timestamp
- Cross-provider deduplication using hash lookup in Redis bloom filter
- Configurable similarity threshold for near-duplicate detection

### Observability
- Structured JSON logging with correlation IDs
- OpenTelemetry tracing for distributed request tracking
- Prometheus metrics endpoint at `/metrics`
- Key metrics: sync_jobs_total, sync_duration_seconds, photos_processed_total, provider_errors_total

# Photo Import/Sync Microservice Specification

## 1. Problem Statement

Photographers need to import and synchronize their existing photo libraries from multiple cloud storage providers (Google Photos, iCloud, Dropbox, Amazon Photos, OneDrive) into RawDrive. Currently, users must manually download and re-upload photos, which is time-consuming and error-prone. A dedicated microservice will automate this process with provider-specific adapters, job queuing, and incremental sync capabilities.

## 2. User Story

As a **professional photographer**, I want to **connect my existing cloud storage accounts and automatically import my photos into RawDrive**, so that **I can consolidate my photo library without manual downloads and uploads**.

## 3. Acceptance Criteria

### Happy Path - OAuth Connection
- **GIVEN** a user is on the import settings page
- **WHEN** they click "Connect Google Photos"
- **THEN** they are redirected to Google's OAuth consent screen
- **AND** upon approval, their credentials are securely stored
- **AND** they see a success confirmation with provider status

### Happy Path - Full Sync
- **GIVEN** a user has connected a provider
- **WHEN** they initiate a full sync job
- **THEN** all photos are enumerated and downloaded
- **AND** progress is reported in real-time (processed/total/errors)
- **AND** photos are stored with extracted EXIF metadata
- **AND** duplicates are detected and skipped

### Happy Path - Incremental Sync
- **GIVEN** a user has previously completed a full sync
- **WHEN** they trigger an incremental sync
- **THEN** only new/modified photos since last sync are processed
- **AND** the sync completes significantly faster than full sync

### Edge Case - Rate Limiting
- **GIVEN** a provider returns a rate limit error (429)
- **WHEN** the sync worker encounters this error
- **THEN** it applies exponential backoff with jitter
- **AND** retries up to 5 times before failing the photo
- **AND** continues with remaining photos

### Edge Case - Token Expiration
- **GIVEN** a provider's access token has expired
- **WHEN** an API call fails with 401
- **THEN** the service automatically refreshes the token
- **AND** retries the original request
- **AND** updates stored credentials

### Edge Case - Large Library (100K+ photos)
- **GIVEN** a user has 100,000+ photos in their library
- **WHEN** they start a full sync
- **THEN** the job processes photos in batches
- **AND** can be paused/resumed without data loss
- **AND** completes within reasonable time via horizontal scaling

### Error Handling - Provider Unavailable
- **GIVEN** a provider's API is down
- **WHEN** sync attempts fail after max retries
- **THEN** the job is marked as failed with clear error message
- **AND** partial progress is preserved
- **AND** user is notified via webhook/email

### Error Handling - Invalid Credentials
- **GIVEN** a user's OAuth tokens are revoked
- **WHEN** refresh token fails
- **THEN** the provider status is marked as disconnected
- **AND** user is prompted to re-authenticate
- **AND** pending jobs for that provider are cancelled

## 4. Technical Context

| Aspect | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Service Location | `services/photo-sync-service/` |
| Runtime | Node.js 20 LTS + TypeScript 5.2+ |
| Framework | Fastify 4.x |
| Message Queue | RabbitMQ with amqplib |
| Database | PostgreSQL 16 (shared) + Redis 7 |
| API Gateway | Traefik v3 (priority 130 for `/api/v1/sync/*`) |
| Autoscaling | KEDA with RabbitMQ trigger |
| Docker Image | Multi-stage Alpine (~150MB) |
| Port | 8007 (dev), 8007 (prod) |
| Patterns to Follow | Existing microservices (gallery-service, upload-service) |

## 5. Non-Goals

- **Photo editing/processing** - This service only imports; processing is handled by existing services
- **Two-way sync** - Photos flow into RawDrive only, not back to providers
- **Social media imports** - Instagram, Facebook, etc. are out of scope for v1
- **Real-time sync** - Uses polling/manual trigger, not webhooks for v1
- **Local folder sync** - Only cloud providers, not local filesystem
- **Album/folder structure preservation** - v1 imports photos flat; album mapping is future enhancement

## 6. Implementation Tasks

```tasks
## Phase 11: Testing

- [ ] T058: Create integration tests for OAuth flow | File: services/photo-sync-service/tests/integration/oauth.test.ts
- [ ] T059: Create integration tests for sync job lifecycle | File: services/photo-sync-service/tests/integration/sync-job.test.ts
- [ ] T060: Create load tests for concurrent sync jobs | File: services/photo-sync-service/tests/load/sync-load.test.ts
```

## 7. Success Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| OAuth connection success rate | ≥ 99% for supported providers |
| Full sync throughput | ≥ 100 photos/minute per worker |
| Incremental sync detection | < 30 seconds for delta calculation |
| Duplicate detection accuracy | ≥ 99.5% (hash-based) |
| Service availability | 99.9% uptime |
| API response time (P95) | < 200ms for job status queries |
| Memory usage per pod | < 512MB under load |
| KEDA scaling response | < 60 seconds to scale up |

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Provider API changes break adapters | Version-specific adapter implementations, comprehensive error logging, health checks per provider |
| OAuth token storage security breach | AES-256-GCM encryption at rest, Kubernetes Secrets for keys, audit logging |
| Rate limiting causes sync failures | Per-provider rate limiters, exponential backoff, queue-based throttling |
| Large libraries overwhelm workers | Batch processing, KEDA autoscaling, distributed locks for job coordination |
| iCloud lacks official API | Use CloudKit Web Services with app-specific passwords, document limitations |
| Network failures during downloads | Resumable downloads where supported, checkpointing progress, retry with backoff |
| Duplicate photos across providers | Hash-based deduplication with Bloom filter for O(1) lookup |
| RabbitMQ unavailability | Dead letter queues, health checks, fallback to Redis-based queuing |
